doors.trait: Words come from you without thinking about it first. Your expression flows as if the speaking itself knows where to go, finding gaps in silence and filling them with what lands. Others hear it pouring out and do not see the work. They do not see work because there is none to see.
doors.scene: Eleven in the morning. Your hands are on the keyboard, coffee getting cold nearby. Three colleagues in the message thread ask questions, and you start typing answers that keep coming through your fingers into words. By noon someone has copied what you wrote. Another marks it helpful. You stop because there is nothing left to explain.
doors.outside: People come to you. When silence needs breaking or confusion needs words, you pour what they drink: the story, the joke, the right phrase. You do not think it is work. They do not think you are working. That being feeds them and refills you before you notice the cost.
